title: AI Governance: Ensuring Ethics and Inclusion
summary: Effective AI governance requires a multifaceted approach that prioritizes ethics, inclusivity, and accountability. UNESCO's recommendation on the ethics of artificial intelligence serves as a landmark framework for nations to place human rights at the forefront. Countries are developing national strategies to ensure responsible AI development, but challenges persist in balancing governance with innovation.

Let me first begin with the opportunities. Artificial intelligence has enormous potential to improve administration. We know this because there are efficiencies, for example, studies suggest that nearly two-thirds of administrative tasks from scheduling to compliance checks are repetitive. AI can handle these very reliably forcing staff to focus on higher order work. So imagine immigration officers who can no longer have to be drowned with paperwork, but instead focus on the human dimensions of the cases that they are before them. Also in terms of better decision making, artificial intelligence can help identify trends, whether in case law, backlogs, benefits claims or public health records. So policy makers act on evidence rather than on instinct. In terms of consistency, sorry, in terms of accuracy and consistency, properly designed AI systems can reduce errors that creep into the manual process.
